pointers.sentence: That call is the whole of the interface, and under ASGI the method's asynchronous twin makes the same one (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

After the call it refuses `None` and a coroutine nobody awaited, and nothing else: there is no test that the object returned is an `HttpResponse` (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`).
Each time it is called it makes a new instance of the class, stores the request and the arguments on it, and calls the instance's `dispatch` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

A class with no method for the request's method answers with a 405 that lists the ones it has (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).

A class with no method for the request's method answers with a 405 that lists the ones it has (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).

The handler looks up an **error view** for the status, by default one of the four in `django/views/defaults.py`, and calls it with the request and, for every status but 500, the exception ([The error views](views/errors.md)).
The decorators and mixins that require a login are in `django/contrib/auth/` ([Authentication, sessions and messages](auth.md)).
